Attention: Lauren Heath, Chief Operating Officer
Dear Ms. Heath,

We are glad to confirm that Ashcombe Advisory Partners will lead the investor relations program for {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}, and this letter sets out what the two firms have agreed so that we begin from the same understanding. It is a plain document by design; where the language is careful, that is to be clear rather than cautious. Please read it alongside the conversations of these past weeks, which it is meant to record and not to replace.
The program and how we will run it

Our charge is to help {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}} be understood clearly by the investors, analysts, and reporters who follow the company, and to have it ready to speak in one voice whenever it has something to say. In practice that means shaping the core messages, drafting the announcements and supporting materials as they are needed, and standing with your team on the timing and sequencing of what goes out.

Most of the work will move by email and short calls, with the occasional working session when a decision needs the room. We will follow a plan we set together at the outset and revisit as the year unfolds, since an investor relations calendar rarely survives an earnings date untouched. Where a piece of work falls outside what we have scoped here, we will tell you before we begin it, not after.
Your team at Ashcombe

Michael Morris will lead the engagement day to day, and he will be your first call on strategy and on anything sensitive that wants a considered read. Laura Bradley will carry much of the drafting and keep the moving parts in order, and Michelle Black will manage the announcement timelines and the approvals that sit behind them.

I will stay close to the relationship myself. Any announcement that carries real consequence will have my own review before it leaves our hands, so that a partner has read it and not only signed for it.
How we will keep you informed

You will hear from us on a steady cadence rather than only when something is due, because an investor relations program suffers more from silence than from too much contact. Michael Morris will send a short written status at regular intervals and will always be reachable between them, and we will hold a working session whenever a decision is better made in conversation than in a thread. Each note we send will be tied to the specific piece of work it concerns, so the record stays easy to follow long after the fact.
What we will ask of you

An engagement like this works best when one person on your side can speak for the company on messaging, and we understand that person to be you. We will look to you for timely review of drafts, for early word on anything market-moving before it becomes public, and for access to the leaders whose words we help shape. In return we will keep our asks few and clear, and we will not let a missing approval be the reason an announcement slips.
Fee and commencement

We will begin on {{fact:f:E-2018-001.start}}, and the program is expected to run for roughly nine months from that date. Our fee for the work described above is {{fact:f:E-2018-001.fee}}, fixed for that scope, so that you can plan the year with confidence and call on us without watching a clock.
Fees and payment

The fee of {{fact:f:E-2018-001.fee}} covers the program as scoped and is billed in equal monthly installments across the term, each invoice payable within thirty days of its date. Out-of-pocket costs that we incur on your behalf, such as wire-service fees or print production, will be billed at cost and only with your prior agreement. Work you ask us to take on beyond the agreed scope will be quoted separately and started only once you have approved it.
Term and termination

The engagement runs for the period described above and continues until the program is complete or either firm ends it. Either of us may end it on thirty days' written notice, and you will owe fees only for work performed through the effective date of that notice. On request we will return or destroy your materials promptly and help hand off anything in progress, so that nothing is left stranded.
Confidentiality

We will treat the non-public information you share with us as confidential and use it only for the work you have engaged us to do. Our people are held to the same obligation, and we will not disclose your confidential information outside the firm without your consent, except where the law requires it and then only after we have told you, if we are permitted to. This duty outlasts the engagement itself.
Limitation of liability

We will perform our work with the care and skill you are entitled to expect of an advisor in our field. Our counsel supports your decisions and does not replace your own judgment or that of your legal, accounting, and other professional advisors, and responsibility for what the company says and does publicly remains with the company. To the extent the law allows, our liability arising out of this engagement is limited to the fees paid to us under it, and neither firm will be liable to the other for indirect or consequential losses.
Governing law

This letter and the engagement it describes are governed by the laws of the state in which our firm is organized, and we each agree to resolve any dispute there. Should any part of this letter be found unenforceable, the rest of it will stand.

If this letter reflects what we discussed, please sign below and return a copy to us, and we will be ready to begin on the date noted above. If anything here reads differently from your understanding, tell me and we will settle it before you sign. The next step is a signed copy back to my attention, and Michael Morris will follow that same week to set our kickoff.
With regards,
